source.title: Beyond Static Personas: Situational Personality Steering for Large Language Models
source.authors: Ze-Sheng Wei; Mengxia Li; Zi-Lei Wang; Yang Deng

record.file_problem: No apparent file problem; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study identifies and steers persona neurons as a tool for situational personality control, but does not test whether neurons have one or a small number of understandable jobs, or test the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures topic-related neuron activation patterns and their layer distribution. Its personality-steering benchmark results evaluate IRIS, not neuron interpretability or the listed versions, so they are not recorded as rows. The preliminary analyses use contrastive prompts instructing positive and negative personality traits.
record.test_reason: The study locates 'persona neurons' by activation-probability differences under instructed positive/negative personality prompts and uses them to steer personality. It never explains individual neurons, never estimates shares of monosemantic or polysemantic neurons, never scores explanations on held-out text, and never builds attribution graphs. Its neuron analyses (PCA, layer counts, LDA clustering) describe population activation patterns of a selected neuron set, not whether neurons have one main job. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that persona-neuron activations depend on situation, with consistent patterns within a situation. They use this to motivate IRIS, which they report outperforms prompt and steering baselines across benchmarks, architectures and Qwen3 scales.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive positive and negative personality prompts to identify persona neurons by activation-probability differences, then retrieves and steers them. It does not test explanations on held-out activations as in the neuron-explanation methods named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Topic choice changes persona-neuron distributions; the paper reports a maximum layer-wise proportion difference of 2.23% in layer 16.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B, neurons selected by instructed personality contrasts vary in activation pattern and layer distribution with situational topic. Questions on the same topic cluster together.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona-associated FFN neuron sets shift systematically with conversational topic, and similar topics recruit similar neuron sets.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The neuron analyses use instructed positive and negative personality prompts. The text does not state the model used for the situation-behavior clustering result, and several layer-distribution results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. No listed claim version is directly tested.
record.rows_left_out: IRIS benchmark comparisons, hyperparameter studies, and general-capability results were not extracted: they evaluate the paper's steering method or its side effects rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: No share of neurons with one, two or unknown jobs; Qwen3-32B not studied.
Qwen3 0.6B/8B/14B, Llama and Gemma are used only for steering benchmarks, not for interpretability shares.
No interpretable-neuron shares and no tool or architecture comparison. The SiLU vs GeLU contrast concerns steering performance only.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No test of explanations against held-out activations.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 / uses_without_test classification is right. The study treats neurons as steerable units identified by activation-probability thresholds. It does not test whether individual neurons are interpretable. The 'observed' row states describe the paper's own findings, not any claim version, so I set them to cannot_determine relative to the versions. The rows could arguably be dropped, since they are partly selection outputs.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the proportion of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs; does not test explanations on held-out activations.
Tests personality steering across some model sizes and architectures, not whether the claimed shares of interpretable neuron poles hold across models or scale.
Does not examine InceptionV1 or the cat-and-car example.
Does not estimate interpretable-neuron shares or test whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain them.
Does not evaluate attribution graphs or reconstruction error.
Does not test explanations against where neurons activate on new examples.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: PCA of topic-specific and global persona-neuron activation feature vectors

conditions.value: situational topics within Big Five personality domains

rows.measure: Euclidean distances in PCA space and topic clustering
rows.baseline: Global persona neurons; distances between distinct personality domains
rows.value: Maximum distance between topics within one domain is comparable to the distance between distinct personality domains; nearby points correspond to semantically similar topics.
rows.note: The text describes systematic topic-related variation in the activation representations; it does not assess whether individual neurons have one understandable job.
rows.check: Population-level PCA of persona-neuron activation vectors. It says nothing about per-neuron interpretability. The 'observed' state refers to the study's own finding, not to any claim version.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer-wise distributions of situational persona neurons across topics
rows.value: A maximum difference of 2.23% was observed in layer 16; the middle layers had the highest concentration across topics.
rows.note: The text gives the maximum difference and layer but does not explicitly name the model for that particular difference; the figure and appendix include Llama-3-8B-Instruct layer distributions.
rows.check: Layer proportions of selected neurons (max difference 2.23% at layer 16) are counts produced by the selection procedure, not a measure of neuron jobs. Figure 8 confirms the subject is Llama-3-8B-Instruct.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared counts of situational persona neurons across layers and topics
rows.note: The appendix states that the neuron distributions are shown and that persona neurons are most densely concentrated in the middle and final layers.
rows.check: Figure-only count distribution of neurons selected by the paper's thresholding, i.e. a selection output. No bearing on any version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared counts of situational persona neurons across layers and topics
rows.note: The appendix states that the neuron distributions are shown and that persona neurons are most densely concentrated in the middle and final layers.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Applied PCA followed by LDA to persona-neuron activation feature vectors for questions from four topics

conditions.value: four topics within one personality domain

rows.measure: Clustering of activation feature vectors by topic
rows.value: Questions from the same topic formed distinct and cohesive clusters; some clusters overlapped, which the paper attributes to semantic correlations.
rows.note: The study does not identify the model used for this analysis in the text describing this result.
rows.check: Topic clustering of activation vectors after PCA and LDA. The model is unstated (likely Llama-3-8B-Instruct, the paper's primary model). This concerns topic structure in a neuron population, not per-neuron explanations.
